story.title: Why this exists
story.p1: Every board comes with its own app, its own login and its own logbook. Climb a Kilter at your gym and a MoonBoard on holiday and you have two histories that never meet.
story.p2: Then one of those apps vanished overnight and climbers lost their logbooks with it. That is what happens when one company owns the only way into hardware you already paid for.
story.link: What happened, and how to get your data out

who.title: Who builds it
who.body: It started in 2024 with one climber and a repo, and it is still the kind of project people work on in the evenings. Bugs get found by someone standing at the wall, not by a QA team.

next.title: What's next
next.body: More boards, better offline, and getting your data out as easily as it went in. The roadmap is public and the arguments about it happen on Discord.

why.p2: We promise not to enshittify Boardsesh, and self-hosting will always be an option. If you get something out of it and can spare it, chipping in keeps the lights on.

intro.title: Legal & Intellectual Property Policy
intro.p1: Boardsesh is a free, open-source, community-built alternative for browsing and interacting with standardised LED climbing training boards (Kilter Board, Tension Board, MoonBoard, and others). It is non-commercial and maintained entirely by volunteers.
intro.p2: We believe climbers should have the freedom to choose how they interact with hardware they've purchased, and that community-created data should remain accessible to the community.

facts.title: Climbs are factual data
facts.p1: A climb on a standardised board is a list of hold positions on a fixed, standardised layout (e.g. "start on A5, use B12, C3, D18, finish on K11"), combined with a grade and wall angle. This is factual, functional information — comparable to a chess position, a set of GPS coordinates, or a phone number — not a creative work of authorship.
facts.p2: Under U.S. copyright law, facts are not copyrightable (Feist Publications, Inc. v. Rural Telephone Service Co., 499 U.S. 340 (1991)). A standardised board with a finite number of holds (typically 200–500) produces climb definitions that are inherently constrained, factual, and functional.

community.title: The database is community-created
community.p1: The climb databases for these boards are almost entirely user-generated content. Individual climbers create and submit climbs. The board manufacturers did not author this content — they provide a platform for submission and display.
community.p2: The licensing position varies by manufacturer, but in no case does a manufacturer own the community's climb data:
community.aurora: Aurora Climbing (Kilter Board, Tension Board, and others): Aurora's Terms of Use grant them a "perpetual, unrestricted, unlimited, non-exclusive, irrevocable license" over user-submitted content. Crucially, this license is non-exclusive — it does not transfer ownership to Aurora, nor does it prevent the original creator (or third parties) from independently using, collecting, or presenting the same factual data.
community.moonBody: As of the last review of Moon Climbing's public-facing legal documents (February 2026), we did not find app-specific Terms of Service, an End User License Agreement, or a contributed-content license governing the MoonBoard app or its climb database. As with every board here, our position rests on the principle above: climb definitions are factual, functional data, and the databases are community-created.

compilation.title: Comprehensive databases have weak compilation protection
compilation.body: Even where a database arrangement might qualify for thin copyright protection as a compilation, the U.S. Supreme Court has held that protection extends only to creative selection or arrangement — not to the underlying facts. A database that comprehensively collects all user submissions without editorial curation (as these platforms do) is analogous to an alphabetical phone directory, which the Court found unprotectable in Feist.

attribution.title: Attribution & Respect for Creators
attribution.intro: We respect the climbing community and the people who create climbs.
attribution.item1: Where climb creator information is available, we attribute the creator by their username.
attribution.item2: We do not claim authorship of climbs we did not create.
attribution.item3Start: If you are the creator of a climb and would like it removed, please
attribution.item3End: or contact us and we will honour your request promptly.

interop.title: Interoperability & Hardware Compatibility
interop.intro: This project provides software and hardware designs that are compatible with standardised climbing board hardware. Climbers who have purchased these boards have a right to use third-party software and controllers with their own hardware.

software.title: Software interoperability
software.body: Our app communicates with board controllers over standard Bluetooth protocols. The Bluetooth communication protocol used by these boards is unencrypted and based on commodity hardware (WS2812B addressable LEDs driven by standard Bluetooth controllers). Implementing a compatible Bluetooth interface for the purpose of interoperability is well-established as lawful under both U.S. and EU law (Sega Enterprises Ltd. v. Accolade, Inc., 977 F.2d 1510 (9th Cir. 1992); EU Directive 2009/24/EC, Article 6).

controller.title: Open-source controller
controller.p1: This project also offers open-source controller hardware and firmware designs. The controller is an independent, original implementation that communicates using the same Bluetooth protocol as the official controllers. It is built on commodity components (standard microcontrollers and WS2812B LEDs) and does not incorporate any proprietary firmware, code, or hardware designs from any board manufacturer. No patents are known to exist covering the LED controller systems used by any current board manufacturer.
controller.p2: Our controller is designed to be interoperable with both this project's software and, at the user's discretion, official manufacturer apps. Any such interoperability is initiated by the end user on their own hardware.

trademark.title: Trademark Usage
trademark.body: We use board and product names (e.g. "Kilter Board", "MoonBoard", "Tension Board") solely to describe hardware compatibility and interoperability. These names are trademarks of their respective owners. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Aurora Climbing, Moon Climbing, or any board manufacturer.

dmca.title: DMCA & Takedown Requests
dmca.intro: We take intellectual property concerns seriously. If you believe any material in this project infringes your copyright, please contact us with the following information:
dmca.item1: Identification of the copyrighted work you believe is infringed.
dmca.item2: Identification of the material you believe is infringing, with enough detail for us to locate it.
dmca.item3: Your contact information (name, address, email, phone number).
dmca.item4: A statement that you have a good faith belief that the use is not authorised by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.item5: A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information in your notice is accurate and that you are the copyright owner or authorised to act on their behalf.
dmca.review1: We will review all valid requests promptly and in good faith. We may also file a counter-notice where we believe a takedown request is based on a misidentification of the material or a misunderstanding of the law.

community.title: A Note to the Community
community.p1: The climbing community has a long tradition of openly sharing beta. This project exists in that spirit. We are not trying to harm any company — we are trying to give climbers better tools to interact with hardware they already own and data they helped create.
community.p2: Manufacturers continue to benefit from this ecosystem. Our project drives demand for their physical products (holds, boards, panels) where they provide genuine value. We simply believe climbers deserve a choice in how they interact with their hardware.
community.p3: If you are a board manufacturer and would like to discuss collaboration or have concerns, we welcome open dialogue. Please reach out.

legal.footer: This document is provided for informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. Last updated: 08-02-2026

hero.title: Help
hero.subtitle: Short guides for the Boardsesh app, what this site does, how to bring your Kilter or Tension logbook across, and where to ask when you are stuck.

web.title: On this site
web.intro: Everything on boardsesh.com opens in a browser with no install and no sign-in, so any page here is a link you can send to a friend.
web.item1: Look up a climb and see its grade, setter, ascents and beta videos.
web.item2: Browse a board's whole catalog by layout, size and angle.
web.item3: Share a climb, a playlist or your profile as a plain link.
web.item4: Find gyms with boards near you.

app.title: In the app
app.intro: Anything that touches the wall or your logbook happens in the app.
app.item1: Build a queue and work through it with your crew.
app.item2: Run a live session so everyone's phone drives the same queue.
app.item3: Light up holds over Bluetooth on Kilter, Tension and MoonBoard walls.
app.item4: Log your sends and attempts, and attach beta videos to climbs.

aurora.title: Bring your Kilter or Tension logbook
aurora.intro: Link your board account once in the app and your sends come across.
aurora.item1: Tap your avatar, then Settings. On the More screen, tap Connected apps. Under Board Accounts, tap Link on the Tension card, or Sign in to Kilter on the Kilter card, and enter the username and password you use for that board.
aurora.item2: Used the old Kilter app before it shut down? The Kilter (Aurora) card takes a JSON export of your data instead, or points you to Aurora to request it.
aurora.item3: Sync runs one way, from their apps into Boardsesh, about every 12 hours. Nothing you log in Boardsesh is sent back to Kilter or Tension.

climbCounts.title: Why does Kilter's app show more climbs?
climbCounts.intro: Both apps have the same climbs and count them differently.
climbCounts.item1: Boardsesh counts each climb once. The note under the Show button in the filter sheet says the same thing.
climbCounts.item2: Kilter's app appears to count a climb once for every angle it has been climbed at, so a climb with ascents at 40° and 45° counts twice.
climbCounts.item3: On an 8x12 Kilter home wall that comes to about 18,000 climbs in Boardsesh and about 36,000 in Kilter's app.

ask.intro: The Discord is the fastest place to get an answer. Other climbers and the people who build Boardsesh are both in there.

hero.title: Make a playlist and climb it in order
hero.subtitle: Save the climbs you want to come back to, then load the whole list into your queue on board night.

build.title: Make a playlist
build.intro: Playlists live on the Discover tab, and each one belongs to one board.
build.step1: Open Discover. The board pill at the top is the board your new playlist will belong to, so switch it first if you need to.
build.step2: Tap the plus. Give the playlist a name and a color, add a description if you want, then tap Create.
build.step3: It shows up under My Playlists. To add an emoji or make it public, open the playlist and choose Edit details.
build.p1: Add climbs from any list of climbs. Swipe a row to the left, or press and hold it and tap Add to Playlist. The picker is a checklist, so you can tick several playlists for one climb.
build.p2: The picker only shows playlists for the board and layout the climb belongs to. A Tension playlist never fills up with Kilter climbs.
build.shotAlt: The Discover tab showing pinned playlists and the lists Boardsesh builds
build.shotCaption: Discover runs Pinned, then My Playlists, then For You.
build.playlistShotAlt: A playlist with its climbs and the owner controls
build.playlistShotCaption: On your own playlist you can pin it, edit it, and reorder or remove climbs.

remove.title: Take a climb back out
remove.intro: You can remove a climb from the climb itself or from inside the playlist.
remove.p1: From the climb, open Add to Playlist again and tap the playlist that has a tick. The tick clears and the climb is out.
remove.p2: From the playlist, tap the pencil in the toolbar, or open the ⋯ menu and choose Reorder & remove climbs. Each climb gets a red minus on the left and a drag handle on the right. Tap the minus and confirm Remove climb? to take it out. Drag the handle to change the order. Tap Done when you're finished.
remove.p3: The lists under For You have no edit mode, because you didn't put anything in them by hand. Change what feeds them instead. Un-heart a climb and it leaves Liked Climbs. Log the send and it leaves Projects.

queue.title: Climb the whole list
queue.intro: Tap a climb in a playlist and your queue becomes that playlist.
queue.p1: The tap opens the climb and replaces your queue with the playlist in order, starting from the climb you tapped, so swiping in the play drawer walks the list. If you had climbs queued after your current one, a Start playlist? sheet asks first and tells you how many will drop out. The play button in the playlist header (Queue every climb) does the same from the top.
queue.p2: In a session with other people, tapping a climb only opens it for you. The shared queue and the wall stay as they were.
queue.sessionsLink: How a session shares one queue

smart.title: The eight lists Boardsesh builds for you
smart.intro: They sit under For You on Discover and update on their own.
smart.crowdFavorites: Crowd Favorites: well-rated climbs on your board with plenty of sends that you haven't sent yet.
smart.hiddenGems: Hidden Gems: climbs rated 4.5 stars or better that only a handful of people have sent.
smart.atYourLevel: At Your Level: popular climbs around the grade you've been sending.
smart.fresh: Fresh: climbs published recently on your board, with the most followed setters first.
smart.fiveStars: Five Stars: climbs you rated five stars.
smart.mostRepeated: Most Repeated: climbs you've logged more than one attempt on, most attempts first.
smart.projects: Projects: climbs you've logged but never sent, most attempts first.
smart.likedClimbs: Liked Climbs: every climb you've hearted.
smart.p1: The first four read your board's catalog at your angle, only count climbs your hold sets can build, and skip anything you've already sent at that angle. The last four come from your own ticks and hearts, so they fill up as you climb.
smart.p2: Hearted a climb mid-session and lost track of it? Open Liked Climbs. The heart on a climb row is what puts it there.
smart.p3: Tap the pin on any card to move it into Pinned at the top of Discover. Pinned playlists follow your account. Pinned For You lists stay on this phone.

tags.title: See which playlists a climb is already in
tags.p1: Tap your avatar, then Settings. On the More screen, scroll to Display and turn on Show playlist tags. Rows on the Climbs tab that are in a playlist grow an extra line with up to two playlist chips and a +N for the rest. Rows in no playlist look the same as before.
tags.p2: The chips are labels. Tapping one doesn't open the playlist. Use Discover for that.

hero.title: Live sessions with your crew
hero.subtitle: Start a session, share the link, and everyone's phone works the same queue. Browsing on your phone never changes what's lit for the others.

start.title: Start a session
start.intro: Every session starts from the Record tab.
start.step1: Open the Record tab. Check the board at the top is the one you're standing at.
start.step2: Leave Show this session live on if you want your crew and climbers at this board to see it and join. Turn it off and only people with your invite link can get in.
start.p1: Until then your queue is a solo queue and lives only on your phone. The Start a session buttons on the Home tab and in the board sheet bring you to this same screen.
start.p2: Once it's live, tap Invite climbers. A QR code comes up with Copy link and Share under it. Anyone who scans the code or opens the link lands on your session.
start.shotAlt: A live session with its crew and shared queue
start.shotCaption: The session screen shows who has joined and what's queued and lit.
start.liveShotAlt: The Climbing now rail listing live sessions
start.liveShotCaption: Climbing now on the Home tab lists live sessions you can join with one tap.

join.title: Join a session
join.intro: There are three ways in, and none of them needs a code.
join.p1: All three open the same card, Join Sam's session?, with the board, the angle and how many people are climbing. Nothing changes on your phone until you tap Join session. If you're already in a session, the app asks first: Leave your current session?
join.way1: Scan the host's QR code with your camera, or open the link they sent you.
join.way2: On the Home tab, look under Climbing now. It lists live sessions from climbers you follow and from boards you follow or have selected.
join.way3: Tap the board at the top of the Climbs tab to open Now on the wall, then scroll to Climbing here now for sessions running on the wall in front of you.

queue.title: One queue, every phone
queue.intro: Everyone in the session can change it.
queue.p1: Add a climb and it shows up on every phone in the session, with your avatar on the row so the crew knows whose pick it is. Anyone can add climbs, drag them into a new order, or remove them.
queue.p2: Ending the session for everyone is for the climber who started it. Everyone else taps Leave session and the session keeps running for the rest. If one of your changes doesn't go through, the app reloads the queue from the crew and says so: Queue was out of sync. Refreshed from your crew.

wall.title: Who lights the wall
wall.intro: One phone holds the board, and nobody has to pass it around.
wall.p1: A board accepts one Bluetooth connection at a time, so the first phone to connect keeps it. On every other phone the lightbulb changes job. Preview a climb and tap the bulb, and the connected phone lights it for you. The queue bar shows whose wall you're on.
wall.p2: On a wall with no lights the bulb says Take the wall instead. Take it and the crew and the gym screen see which climb you're on. If someone else takes it after you, yours is released without a message.
wall.p3: Put a climb up right after someone else lit theirs and the app checks first: Someone just lit that climb. Put yours up instead? Pick Put mine up or Keep theirs.
wall.bluetoothLink: Connecting to a board, and what to do when it fails

crowd.title: Browsing without moving the wall
crowd.intro: As soon as someone else is in your session, swiping is look-only.
crowd.p1: With one other climber in the session, swiping through climbs in the play drawer stops lighting the board. A Browsing pill appears at the top. Tap it and it says: You're just looking. The wall stays where it is. When you do want the wall, tap Put on the wall in the row underneath. The first time this happens in a session, a short notice explains it.
crowd.p2: Climbing alone and want the same? While connected, hold the lightbulb and turn off Light problems on swipe and Light problems when tapping the list.
crowd.p3: So four people can flick through the catalog while the fifth pulls on, and nobody's holds go dark mid-burn.
crowd.previewLink: Preview a climb from any list

history.title: Sessions on your profile
history.intro: Finished sessions are saved to your profile.
history.p1: The Sessions tab on your profile lists every session you've climbed: the climbs, the sends, and when. Nobody can join a finished session and there's no invite link.
history.p2: When you end a session you get a summary screen with Save to Apple Health and Share to Strava on it. To send every session automatically, tap your avatar, then Settings, then Connected apps.

hero.title: Find climbs by hold, region or setter
hero.subtitle: The Climbs tab can narrow the list to one hold, one part of the wall or one setter. This page shows where each filter lives and what it does.

start.title: Grade and angle first
start.intro: Set these before anything else. They change every number in the list.
start.p1: The Grade pill sits next to the search field. Tap a grade to show only that grade. Tap a second grade within three seconds and you get the range between them. Tap the selected grade again and it clears back to Any.
start.p2: Angle is not a filter. It belongs to the board you are on, and every grade and send count in the list is read at that angle. Tap the chip showing the current degrees to change it. A board with a fixed angle has no angle chip.
start.p3: When you are signed in, the Progress chips filter by your own history. Unsent hides everything you have sent. Projects keeps only climbs you have tried and not sent. Not tried keeps climbs you have never logged a go on, and Sent shows the ones you have.

holds.title: Filter by hold
holds.intro: Open Filters, scroll to The climb and tap Hold types.
holds.p1: The board fills the screen. Pinch to zoom and drag to pan, then mark holds:
holds.step1: Pick Include or Exclude. Include means the climb must use the hold. Exclude means it must not.
holds.step2: Pick a hold type: Start, Hand, Finish, Foot or Any.
holds.step3: Tap holds on the board. Tap a hold again with the same brush to clear that mark.
holds.p2: A hold can carry more than one mark, so you can ask for a climb that starts on one hold and finishes on another. Clear all in the top corner removes every mark. Go back and the Filters sheet picks up your holds.
holds.p3: MoonBoard has no foot-only holds, so there is no Foot brush there. Start, Hand, Finish and Any still work.
holds.shotAlt: The hold filter screen with holds marked on the board
holds.shotCaption: Tap a hold to mark what it has to be.
holds.zoneShotAlt: A region box drawn over part of the board
holds.zoneShotCaption: Drag the box or a corner to set the region.

zone.title: Box off part of the wall
zone.intro: Open Filters, scroll to The climb and tap Board region.
zone.p1: Tap Add a region and a box lands on the board. Drag the middle to move it and drag a corner to resize it. With All holds selected, only climbs that sit entirely inside the box stay in the list. Switch to Any hold to keep any climb that reaches into the box.
zone.p2: Clear region removes the box. Hold and region filters run on the server, so on a downloaded board with no signal the list shows a Clear filter button instead of results.

setters.title: Follow setters, then search only them
setters.intro: Following remembers a setter. The Setters screen filters the list.
setters.p1: Follow sits at the top of a setter's page and on every row of the Setters screen, which you open from Filters under The climb. Once you follow a few setters, turn on Climbs by people I follow, just below the Setters row, and the whole search narrows to their climbs. Following a climber counts their linked board accounts too.
setters.p2: The Setters screen is also a picker. Check a box to filter the list to those setters, or tap a name to browse everything they have set. When you are signed in, switch between All setters and Following to choose from a shorter list. The button at the bottom shows how many climbs match and applies the filter.
setters.shotAlt: The Setters screen with checkboxes and Follow buttons
setters.shotCaption: Check a box to filter the list. Tap a name to browse.

rows.title: What a climb row can do
rows.intro: Every climb list has two swipes and a long press.
rows.p1: Swipe a row to the right to add the climb to your queue. Swipe it to the left to open the playlist picker. Neither one lights the board.
rows.p2: The small glyph on a row is your history with that climb. A bolt means you flashed it, a circled tick means you sent it, and a circled cross means you tried it. A circled C marks a benchmark.
rows.actionsLink: See everything in the long-press menu
rows.p3: Press and hold a row for the action menu. Add to queue, Add to Playlist, Log a tick, Add beta video and Copy link all live there.

keep.title: Keep the filters you use
keep.intro: Pin a filter and it sits above the list as a chip.
keep.p1: Most filters in the Filters sheet have a small pin next to their name. Tap it and that filter joins the chip row above the list, so next session it is one tap away. Tap the pin again to take it off.
keep.p2: The button at the bottom of the sheet shows how many climbs match before you apply anything. Reset at the top clears the lot. Each climb counts once, not once per angle.

next.title: Keep going
next.climbActions: What a long press on a climb gets you
next.playlists: Save what you find into a playlist

hero.title: Log a send, then change it later
hero.subtitle: Tick a climb from the board in two taps. Come back any time to change the grade, stars, tries or status, or to delete the entry.

log.title: Log it at the wall
log.intro: The tick button under the board is the quickest way.
log.p1: The big tick button in the middle of the play drawer's action bar opens the log sheet for the climb you are on. The queue bar has a Log ascent button that opens the same sheet. Date and Time are filled in as now and you can change them. Grade, Stars, Tries and Note are optional.
log.p2: Two buttons close the sheet. Attempt logs a go that did not stick. The other button reads Flash when you have never logged this climb at this angle and Tries is still 1. Otherwise it reads Send. With no connection, or before your logbook has loaded, it stays on Send.
log.shotAlt: A climb lit on the board with the tick button below it
log.shotCaption: The tick button opens the log sheet for the climb on the board.
log.logbookShotAlt: The logbook list of logged ascents
log.logbookShotCaption: Swipe a row right to edit it, left to delete it.

edit.title: Change an entry you already logged
edit.intro: Every field is open, including grade, stars and status.
edit.p1: Your logbook is on the Profile tab under Logbook. Swipe a row to the right and the edit sheet opens. You can also press and hold the row and pick Edit logbook entry. A plain tap opens the climb itself. The edit sheet has more fields than the log sheet:
edit.field1: Status: Flash, Send or Attempt. A send you logged as an attempt can be promoted.
edit.field2: Angle and Tries. Date and time stay as you logged them.
edit.p2: If one row bundles several goes from the same day, the app first asks Which entry to edit?
edit.p3: Editing and deleting need a connection. A new tick saves offline and syncs when you are back online. A change to an old one goes straight to the server.

delete.title: Delete an entry
delete.intro: Swipe the row to the left.
delete.p1: Swipe a logbook row to the left, or open the entry and tap Delete this ascent at the bottom of the edit sheet. Both ask you to confirm, because a delete cannot be undone.
delete.p2: Deleting an ascent removes its comments and votes and recounts your stats. A beta video attached to it stays on the climb but no longer points at that ascent.

repeats.title: Attempts, sends and repeats
repeats.intro: How several goes on one climb turn into rows.
repeats.p1: The logbook shows one row per climb, per day, per angle. Four goes on the same problem tonight are one row with the tries added up and the best result showing: a bolt for a flash, a tick for a send, or a circle and the label Project when it did not go. Climb it mirrored and those goes get their own row.
repeats.p2: Come back to it next week and that is a new row. Repeats stay visible. Nothing folds into one lifetime entry.

find.title: Find an old entry
find.p1: The search field at the top matches climb names. Filter opens a sheet with a Latest or Hardest sort, a Status choice of Sends, Attempts or Both, a Flash only switch, a grade range, Min angle and Max angle, a date range and Benchmarks only. There is no board filter. The logbook holds every board at once.
find.p2: Sends from your Kilter or Tension board account come across once you link it. Tap your avatar, then Settings, then Connected apps. Used the old Kilter app from Aurora? Import the JSON export Aurora sends you instead.

next.title: Keep going
next.climbActions: Log a tick from any climb in a list
next.betaVideos: Pin a beta video to what you just logged

hero.title: Connect your phone to the board
hero.subtitle: Tap the lightbulb, pick your board, and your climb lights up. This page covers what to do when that fails, how to tell two boards apart, and how to turn the lights off again.

connect.title: Connect
connect.intro: Tap the lightbulb to pick a board.
connect.p1: The lightbulb sits in the play drawer's action bar and in the top bar of most screens. On the Climbs tab, the board chip on the queue bar does the same job. Tap it and Select Board lists the boards advertising nearby, strongest signal first, with each board's name, its serial number and three signal bars.
connect.p2: Tap yours. The app connects and lights the climb you're on. The bulb fills whenever the wall is lit, by your phone or by another phone in your session. The first time, iOS asks for Bluetooth. Android 12 and newer asks for nearby devices. Android 11 and older asks for Location, because that's the only way older Android lets an app see Bluetooth scan results.
connect.shotAlt: The Select Board sheet listing nearby boards
connect.shotCaption: Select Board lists the strongest signal first, each row with its serial.
connect.litShotAlt: A climb lit on the board in the play drawer
connect.litShotCaption: A filled bulb means the wall is lit, by you or by your crew.
connect.p3: At a different wall? Change board is the first row of the menu behind your avatar. The board at the top of the Climbs tab opens Now on the wall, which has Switch board at the bottom.

hidden.title: Hold the lightbulb
hidden.intro: The board controls live behind a long press.
hidden.p1: While your phone is connected, press and hold the lightbulb, or the board chip on the queue bar. A sheet opens with these controls, top to bottom:
hidden.row1: Auto-disconnect. When on, your phone lets go of the board after a set idle time so someone else can connect. The default is 30 seconds. To change it, tap your avatar, then Settings, and find the Auto-disconnect section.
hidden.row2: Light the hold above. Adds a dimmer LED above each lit start and hand hold. MoonBoard controllers only, so it won't appear on a Kilter or Tension board.
hidden.row3: Light problems on swipe. Lights the board as you swipe between climbs in the play drawer.
hidden.row4: Light problems when tapping the list. Lights the board when you pick a climb from a list. Turn this and the one above off and browsing stops changing the wall.
hidden.row5: Re-light board. Pushes the current climb to the LEDs again if a hold drops out.
hidden.row6: Turn off all lights. The board goes dark and your phone stays connected.
hidden.row7: Disconnect board. Use this when you connected to the wrong wall.
hidden.p2: Holding the bulb while disconnected does nothing. A short tap connects, straight back to the last board you used.

failed.title: When it won't connect
failed.intro: The Couldn't connect alert names the problem. Find yours below.
failed.fix1: Couldn't find your board. Check the board is on and you're near it. If another phone is connected to it, disconnect there first. A board takes one phone at a time.
failed.fix2: Couldn't connect. Move closer to the board and tap the bulb again.
failed.fix3: Connected, but the board didn't respond. The controller is stuck. Turn the board off and on, then try again.
failed.fix4: Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and tap the bulb again.
failed.fix5: Couldn't connect to your board. Anything else that went wrong. Tap the bulb again. If it keeps happening, turn Bluetooth off and on.
failed.p1: On Android, if Select Board finds no boards at all, a note appears at the bottom of the sheet. Android 12 and newer needs Location allowed before it shows scan results. Android 11 and older needs the Location toggle on. Tap Allow Location or Turn on Location, close the sheet, and tap the bulb again.
failed.p2: If you close Select Board yourself, no alert appears. The app treats it as a cancel.

twoBoards.title: Two boards in range
twoBoards.intro: Read the serial before you tap.
twoBoards.p1: In a gym with two walls, both controllers show up in Select Board. The list puts the strongest signal first, but the bars are read once when a board is first seen and don't update while you stand there. The serial on each row is the reliable clue. A board you've connected to before also shows Last connected and a time under its name.
twoBoards.p2: If the app knows that controller belongs to a different board setup, it stops you first. An alert titled Board configuration doesn't match offers Cancel, Connect anyway and, where it can, Switch board setup. If you're already lit on the wrong wall, hold the lightbulb and tap Disconnect board.

duplicate.title: The same board listed twice
duplicate.intro: Two rows are almost always two boxes.
duplicate.p1: An Aurora controller advertises its name, serial and firmware level together, like Kilter Board#751737@3. Boardsesh shows one row per advertised name, so two rows with different serials are two controllers. A row that reads only Kilter Board, with no serial, is a newer manufacturer-built LED box. Two of those in one gym share a name and collapse into one row, which connects to whichever was seen last.
duplicate.p2: There's no forget-this-device list, because the app keeps no list of devices. It remembers only the last board you connected to, so the lightbulb can reconnect with one tap. Connecting to another board replaces it. Tapping Disconnect board clears it.
duplicate.p3: A board showing twice under Your boards is a different problem. On the boards screen, tap Edit next to Your boards. A board you own gets Delete, a board you follow gets Unfollow. To rename a board you own, tap the pencil on its card without going into Edit.

control.title: When someone else has the board
control.intro: You can still put climbs on the wall.
control.p1: In a session, only one phone connects to the board. On the others, preview a climb and tap the lightbulb, and the connected phone lights it for you. If there's nothing to hand over, the bulb reads Someone else is driving the board.
control.p2: On walls with no lights the same button reads Take the wall. It tells the crew and the gym screen which climb you're on. No Bluetooth involved.

handsFree.title: Next climb without touching the phone
handsFree.intro: Change climbs from the lock screen.
handsFree.p1: On iPhone, a live session puts a Live Activity on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island: the climb's name, its grade, where you are in the queue, and a picture of the board. The phone holding the board also gets Previous and Next buttons, a lightbulb that re-lights the wall, and Mirror climb on boards that support it. A solo queue doesn't get one. Start or join a session first.
handsFree.p2: Android shows the same controls in an ongoing notification called Active climbing session, on the same terms. There's no headphone-button shortcut on either platform.
handsFree.p3: The board stays connected when the screen goes off or you switch apps, so putting the phone down doesn't end anything.

next.title: Keep going
next.findingClimbs: Find something to put on the wall

hero.title: Press and hold a climb
hero.subtitle: Every action on a climb is behind a long press on its row, including Preview, which shows you the climb without lighting the wall.

open.title: Open the menu
open.intro: It works on the Climbs tab, in playlists, in your logbook and in the queue.
open.p1: Press and hold a climb row. It lifts into a card with the climb drawn on its board. Three buttons run across the top: Log a tick, Add to Playlist and Share. The rest of the actions are in the list underneath.
open.p2: If you'd rather tap than hold, the Climbs tab can show a ⋮ button on every row that opens the same card. Tap your avatar, then Settings, scroll to Display and turn on Show quick-actions button.
open.shotAlt: The climb actions card open over a list of climbs
open.shotCaption: The card has three quick buttons on top and the full list below.
open.previewShotAlt: The play drawer in its browsing state
open.previewShotCaption: In Preview, the Browsing pill sits at the top and the commit row underneath.

preview.title: Preview a climb without lighting the board
preview.intro: Preview is the first item in the list.
preview.p1: Preview opens the climb in the play drawer without adding it to your queue. Climbing alone with board lighting on, that's all it does. There is no pill, and your next swipe puts you back on your queue and lights the board as usual.
preview.p2: In a session with other people, or with Light problems on swipe turned off, a Browsing pill sits at the top and a commit row waits underneath. Tap Set active when you want the climb. If a climb is already lit on the wall, the button reads Put on the wall instead. Back to live returns you to your queue.
preview.p3: In a session that means you can read the beta for the next climb while someone else is mid-burn, and nothing you look at reaches the LEDs or moves anyone's queue.
preview.p4: Climbing alone, you get the same behavior from a setting. Hold the lightbulb in the play drawer to open the board controls, then turn off Light problems on swipe and Light problems when tapping the list. Join a session and browsing is on automatically.
preview.sessionsLink: How a session keeps browsing off the wall

quick.title: The three buttons across the top
quick.intro: The three actions you use most.
quick.tick: Log a tick opens the ascent sheet for that climb, so you can log a send from a list without opening the climb.
quick.playlist: Add to Playlist turns the card into a checklist of your playlists. Tick to add, untick to remove.
quick.share: Share hands a link to the climb to your phone's share sheet.
quick.p1: The card closes as soon as an action fires. Add to Playlist is the exception. It stays open so you can tick more than one list.

rest.title: The rest of the list
rest.intro: After Preview, the list runs in this order. Some rows only appear when they apply.
rest.queue: Add to queue: puts the climb after your current one without replacing anything.
rest.favorite: Toggle favorite: the heart. Hearted climbs fill your Liked Climbs list.
rest.editEntry: Edit logbook entry: only when you opened the climb from your logbook.
rest.betaVideo: Add beta video: when you're signed in.
rest.edit: Edit climb: your own climbs, while they're a draft or within 24 hours of publishing.
rest.remix: Remix this climb: starts a new climb from this one's holds, on boards where you can set climbs.
rest.openInAurora: Open in Aurora app: Tension and the other Aurora boards that still have a public climb page. Kilter doesn't.
rest.report: Report climb: when you're signed in and moderation is on.

next.title: Keep going
next.playlists: Playlists and the lists Boardsesh builds for you

hero.title: Attach a beta video to a climb
hero.subtitle: Boardsesh links Instagram reels and TikToks to climbs. This page shows where the beta on a climb lives, how to attach a video you have already posted, and how to film new beta from a climb.

share.title: Attach a video you already posted
share.intro: Share the post from Instagram or TikTok straight into Boardsesh.
share.p1: On your reel or TikTok, tap Share and pick Boardsesh. In Instagram it can be hiding under More. Boardsesh opens a screen called Attach your beta, with the post at the top and your logged climbs below it. There is a search box if the climb you want is not near the top.
share.p2: Tap the climb the video shows. That attaches it straight away and a Beta video attached message confirms it. There is no confirm step and no way to remove a video once it is attached, so check the climb name before you tap. If the caption was written by Boardsesh, the matching climb sits first under Matched from the caption, and the rest of your climbs sit under Your other ascents.
share.p3: You need a Boardsesh account, and the climb has to be in your logbook already. A send or an attempt both count. If you are signed out when you share, sign in and the link is waiting for you. Only Instagram and TikTok links work, and the post has to be public. Boardsesh stores only the link, so the clip stays where you posted it.

find.title: Find the beta on a climb
find.intro: Beta Videos is a section under the board on every climb.
find.p1: Open a climb and scroll down past the board. Below the Logbook section, and the setter's notes if the climb has any, you will see Beta Videos. Each card is a video someone attached to this climb, with their handle on it. Tap a card and it opens in Instagram or TikTok. Boardsesh does not play the video itself.
find.p2: If nobody has attached one yet, the section says so. When you are signed in there is a plus button in the section header. It opens the Share your beta sheet described below.
find.p3: To browse only climbs that have beta, open Filters and turn on Beta videos only. The pin next to it puts a Beta chip on the row above the list, so next time it is one tap.

add.title: Film new beta from a climb
add.intro: Add beta video gives you a caption to post with, then takes the link back.
add.p1: Press and hold a climb and choose Add beta video, or tap the plus in the climb's Beta Videos section. The Share your beta sheet has three steps. Step 1, Copy your caption: the caption has the climb name, angle and board in it, for example "Climb name" @ 40° on the Kilter Board. Tap Copy caption. Step 2, Post it as a reel: tap Open Instagram and post your video with that caption. Open Instagram copies the caption too, in case you skipped step 1.
add.p2: Step 3, Send it back to Boardsesh: share the posted reel to Boardsesh as described above, or copy its link, paste it under Already have a link? at the bottom of the sheet and tap Attach. Either way the video lands on the climb and angle you opened the sheet from.
add.p3: Keep the quoted climb name in the caption. It is how Boardsesh matches the reel to the climb when you share it back. MoonBoard captions are written without quotes, so on a MoonBoard pick the climb from the list yourself.

shelf.title: Your beta on your profile
shelf.intro: Every video you attach is collected on your Profile tab.
shelf.p1: Open the Profile tab and scroll to the bottom of Progress. The Beta videos shelf shows your latest, and See all opens the full set. Other climbers' profiles work the same way. A climber with no beta has no shelf.
shelf.p2: You need an account to attach a video, but anyone can watch one. Send someone a climb link and they see its beta on boardsesh.com without signing in.

docs.headerSubtitle: Complete reference for the Boardsesh REST and WebSocket APIs

overview.title: Boardsesh API Overview
overview.intro: Boardsesh provides two complementary APIs for interacting with interactive climbing training boards (Kilter, Tension):

rest.title: REST API
rest.intro: Use the REST API for stateless operations like searching climbs, fetching board configuration, and user authentication. The REST API is ideal for:
rest.feature4: Resolving URL slugs to numeric IDs

ws.title: WebSocket GraphQL API
ws.intro: Use the WebSocket API for real-time features like party sessions and queue synchronization. The GraphQL API provides:
ws.feature4: All REST API functionality via queries/mutations

auth.title: Authentication
auth.restBody: Uses NextAuth session cookies. Authenticate via
auth.wsBodyEnd: and include it in the connection parameters:

rateLimit.title: Rate Limiting
rateLimit.body: Authentication endpoints are rate-limited to prevent abuse. Rate limit headers are included in responses. Public read endpoints have generous limits.

ws.title: WebSocket Connection Guide
ws.introStart: The Boardsesh WebSocket API uses the

session.title: Session Management
session.body: Sessions are the core collaboration unit. Users join sessions to share a climb queue.

delta.title: Delta Synchronization
delta.body: When reconnecting, use delta sync to catch up without full state transfer:

connectionHandling.title: Connection Handling
connectionHandling.body: The WebSocket connection may be interrupted by network changes. Implement reconnection logic with the graphql-ws retry options and use delta sync to maintain state consistency.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro1: Boardsesh is an open-source app for controlling climbing training boards (Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard) over Bluetooth. This policy explains what data we collect, why, and what we do with it.
privacy.intro2ProductAnalytics: The short version: we collect only what we need to make the app work. We do not sell your data, we do not run ads, and we do not share data with third-party marketers or data brokers.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.accountBody: When you create an account, we store your email address and username. Your email is used for authentication. Your username is displayed on your profile and visible to other users in Party Mode sessions and social features.
collect.activityBody: When you log a send or attempt, we store the climb details, grade, date, and any notes you add. This powers your logbook and progression tracking.
collect.locationBody: If you grant location permission, we use your approximate location to help you discover nearby Party Mode sessions. We do not track your location in the background or store location history.
collect.productAnalyticsBody: We use PostHog and Vercel Analytics to understand feature usage, page views, performance, and where the app is slow. Some signed-in product events are linked to your Boardsesh account so we can understand which features are useful. We do not use this data for ads.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.body: Boardsesh uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to connect to your climbing board's LED controller. The Bluetooth connection is used exclusively to send hold lighting commands to the board. No personal data is transmitted over Bluetooth. The app does not read data from the board beyond basic device identification during pairing.

location.title: Location data
location.body1: Location access is optional. When granted, it is used for one purpose: making your Party Mode session discoverable to nearby climbers. Your location is shared with the server only while a Party Mode session is active. We do not store your location history, build a location profile, or share location data with anyone outside of the party session discovery feature.
location.body2: You can revoke location permission at any time in your device settings. The app works fully without it.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.vercelBody: We use Vercel for hosting and analytics. Vercel processes requests to serve the app and collects anonymous usage metrics. See
thirdParty.posthogBody: We use PostHog for product analytics, including server-side events for native app features like iOS Live Activities. See
thirdParty.auroraBody: If you link your Aurora Climbing account (used by Kilter and Tension boards), we sync your climb data with Aurora's servers so your logbook stays consistent across apps. This sync only happens when you initiate it. See

sharing.title: Data sharing
sharing.body1ProductAnalytics: We do not sell your data. We do not run ads. We do not share your information with third-party marketers or data brokers. The only data shared externally is what is described above (Vercel hosting/analytics, PostHog product analytics, Aurora Climbing sync when you opt in).
sharing.body2: Other Boardsesh users can see your username, profile, and logged climbs if you participate in social features like Party Mode. This is visible in the app and is part of how the product works.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.body: We keep your account data and climb history for as long as your account is active. If you stop using Boardsesh, your data stays until you delete your account.

deletion.title: Account deletion
deletion.intro: You can delete your account and all associated data at any time. There are two ways to do it:
deletion.inAppBody: Open More from your profile, scroll to the bottom, and tap Delete Account. You will be asked to confirm before anything is removed.
deletion.onWebBodyEnd: and open More from your profile to find the same Delete Account button.
deletion.permanent: Deletion is immediate and permanent. Once confirmed, we remove your email address, username, logbook entries, queue data, and party session history from our servers. This cannot be undone.

children.title: Children
children.body: Boardsesh is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If we change this privacy policy, we will update this page with the new text and the "last updated" date. For significant changes, we may also notify you in the app.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body1Start: Questions about this policy or your data? Email us at
contact.body2Start: Boardsesh is open source. You can see exactly what data the app collects and how it is processed by reading the source code on
